summary: I used the remaining time on the one judgment-changing question still reachable: whether the uniform-timer separation I recorded survives the adverse history of a voter that is already campaigning before the leader is isolated. The probe isolates one voter first and waits for it to report Candidate, then isolates the leader together with the nonvoter so the two remaining voters can elect, and polls the leader's verifications while watching for a competing leader; twenty adverse trials are contrasted with two plain uniform controls. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence, and itself informative: no adverse trial produced a higher-term candidacy at all — the isolated voter sat in state Candidate at the leader's own term in every trial, which is pre-vote at work, since a node that cannot reach a majority never increments its term — and no confirmation followed a competing leader in any of the twenty, nor in the two controls. If the retained run reproduces that, it does more than repeat a negative: it explains the uniform-case bound structurally, because a voter cannot campaign for real until a majority is willing to pre-vote for it, and that willingness arrives no earlier than the timers a peer needs to lose the leader — which are at least the leader's lease when the settings are shared. That also sharpens why the mixed-timer configuration is the one path into the defect: a node whose election timer is shorter than the leader's lease is the only one that can get ahead of the lease at all. I declared the overlap prediction as the comparison under test rather than assuming it, so a retained run that fails it returns the twenty adverse trials as explicit witnesses that the separation survives the adverse history, and the plain uniform trials remain the control. Every earlier question stays answered and its evidence untouched; this is a new child question under the confirmation-window work, submitted for a retained execution whose receipt I will interpret if the run's remaining time allows it.
